title: Implement operator JIT RBAC sealer and KMS region annotator
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes:
- Add operator Just-In-Time (JIT) RBAC sealer for ephemeral operator privileges
- Attach KMS region annotations for KMS calls to improve residency auditing and policy enforcement
- Admission controller rejects resources without required residency/KMS annotations when compliance mode is enabled
description:
Motivation: Long-lived operator grants and ambiguous KMS metadata caused compliance friction and made audits noisy. This PR introduces two coordinated features: (1) an operator JIT RBAC 'sealer' that mints short-lived, scoped grants for operator actions and emits sealed audit records; (2) a KMS region annotator that tags KMS invocation metadata with resolved region residency, driving policy decisions and improving post-hoc auditability.

Solution overview: Implement an admission-time policy and an operator-side JIT flow. The admission controller validates resource residency annotations (optional by flag) and rejects creations that would escape residency guarantees when compliance mode is active. The operator sealer provides an API for creating ephemeral role bindings with a bounded TTL and embeds a sealed-audit token (HMAC + timestamp) signed by the cluster attestor key; the audit pipeline consumes and verifies seals. The KMS region annotator hooks into the kms client to attach a region_pin header derived from configured region-resolution logic and includes proof metadata for the audit pipeline.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement admission controller and webhook (k8s) with feature flag support
- [x] Add operator JIT RBAC sealer implementation and controller sidecar shim
- [x] Add KMS client annotator and region resolution logic with a pluggable resolver
- [x] Unit and integration tests for RBAC lifecycle, seal verification, and annotator behavior
- [x] Documentation: compliance guide and migration notes
- [x] Rollout plan (canary on Dedicated then Private)

Review conversation (summary):
- Marco Hernandez: "We need a feature flag and a safe default off for hosted customers. Also request CMS for attestor keys rotation docs."
- Author (Aisha): "Added feature flag runtime.enableJITSealer (default false for hosted). Added docs section on key rotation and operator attestor rotation playbook."
- Priya Shah: "Can we ensure the annotator is idempotent and doesn't double-annotate on retries? Add unit for that."
- Author: "Updated middleware to check existing region_pin header and noop if present; added unit tests. CI flagged a race in controller reconcile; addressed by introducing request coalescing lock and re-ran tests."
- Evan Li: "Approving pending CI green and an e2e run on Dedicated Canary."
- Merge: "Squash and merge after canary: approved."

Testing and CI notes: initial CI run failed (race in controller), fixed in commit 3, subsequent CI run passed. Integration e2e performed in internal Dedicated canary cluster (green).

Rollout and migration:
- Step 1: merge behind feature flag (runtime.enableJITSealer=false).
- Step 2: deploy KMS annotator (no-op if resolver not configured).
- Step 3: enable residency admission in compliance-only Dedicated clusters and monitor audit ingestion error rates.
- Step 4: enable JIT sealer for operator pools with a staged TTL (default 300s) and observability dashboards (rbac.jit.mints, rbac.jit.failures, kms.annotator.hotpath).

Backward compatibility: All changes are feature-flagged and additive. Operators without the sealer continue to use existing long-lived bindings. KMS annotator is safe-guarded against double-annotation. No breaking API changes for customers.

Security considerations: sealed-audit tokens use cluster attestor HMAC key; key rotation instructions included in docs. The admission controller rejects resources that would otherwise violate residency; a migration helper script is included to annotate existing resources for the Private installer.

Related work: ENG-12846 (Linear), SUP-8421 (support escalations on residency audit noise), aligns with prior residency and KMS policy efforts but is focused on operator grants and sealing rather than policy translation.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: runtime.enableJITSealer (default false). Admission toggle: admission.residency.enforce (default false). KMS resolver config: kms.resolver.type (aws|gcp|static) and kms.resolver.map in values.yaml.
